name: Yasuko Mari
voice: Soft, attentive and gently practical. Notices sleeves, uneaten food and tired eyes. Deflects attention by caring for the other person. Small hesitations reveal uncertainty; her humor is quiet. A first-year peer, never the nurse or the MC's mother.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The nurse asks two first-years to prepare a public noticeboard outside the infirmary rest area. No patient records or medical tasks are involved.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: You can use this chair. The other one makes a terrible noise.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You know that from experience?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Everyone knows when someone uses it. That's the difficulty.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She moves her bag off the good chair and notices a loose thread on the MC's cuff.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Ano... your sleeve. It's caught on the button. May I?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Oh. Yes, thanks.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She frees the thread, then steps back before I can feel that I'm being inspected.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Yasuko Mari. Mari is fine. The nurse said we're sorting the public leaflets today.

choices.text: I'm Takahashi. Which pile should I take?

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: The ones with the blue heading. They're easiest to mix up.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I can probably manage that.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Good. If either of us gets confused, we can ask.

choices.text: You seem good at this. I'll let you do the careful parts.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I can. But we were both asked to help, Takahashi-kun. Here—this pile is yours.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant I don't want to get in your way.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then take a pile. That would help more.

choices.text: Thanks for the sleeve. You don't have to look after me while we're working.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I wasn't—ah. I was, wasn't I? You caught me before the leaflets even started.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I can keep track of my own buttons. Usually.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then we'll trust you with the blue leaflets too.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We sort the public information sheets and ask the nurse to check them. The chair squeaks once when the MC forgets which one to use.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: That one.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I understand the warning now.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She covers a small laugh with her hand, as if we're in a library rather than an office with very loud furniture.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We work on noticeboard headings during a long lunch/activity block. Mari has two cloth-wrapped lunch boxes.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Expecting company?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I pack lunches for my siblings in the morning. Sometimes my hands keep going after I've counted everyone.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: So the second one is an administrative error?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: A rather nice one, I hope. You may have it if you like.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She starts explaining every part of the meal before opening her own box.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: Her tea is still sealed. I haven't seen her take a bite.

choices.text: I'd like some. Let's both eat before the headings take over the table.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: They do seem to be multiplying.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll move the scissors. You rescue your lunch.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Thank you. I almost forgot it was getting cold.

choices.text: You should bring an extra one for me every day.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Every day?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: If you already make too much.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I can offer you this one. I don't want that to become a promise I haven't made.

choices.text: Thanks, but I brought lunch. Could you save it for yourself later?

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I could. That hadn't quite occurred to me.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Afternoons are long.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: They are. I'll put it somewhere cool.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We put the work aside for lunch, then finish the headings afterwards.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: I used to be better at making small portions.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You could practice on yourself.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: That sounds oddly difficult when you say it. I'll try.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The nurse permits a break at the visitor table while the noticeboard materials dry. Mari opens a thermos.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Barley tea. Mugicha. No caffeine, if that helps you decide.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You carry an entire drinks menu in there?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Only the part people ask about most often.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She pours a cup for herself and pauses over the spare one.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is it your favorite?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Everyone at home likes it.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She answers automatically, then watches his face. Her fingers tighten slightly around the lid of the thermos.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I asked whether you do.

choices.text: Come on, that shouldn't be a difficult question.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I heard the question. I was thinking.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't mean to put you on the spot.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then please give me a moment.

choices.text: You can think about it. I'm not testing you.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I like the roasted smell. Especially before the first sip.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That sounds like an answer.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: It is, isn't it? Yes. I like it.

choices.text: I'll try a little, if there's enough.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: There is. I brought a spare cup.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Of course you did.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I may be predictable, Takahashi-kun. I have other qualities, I promise. Give me a minute to remember them.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We drink while the paper dries. Mari closes her eyes for a brief, unguarded breath over the warm cup.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: It is the first thing I've seen her enjoy without first checking whether someone else needs it.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: Better while it's warm. We should stop talking about it and drink.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We hang the noticeboard sheets. A classmate asks Mari to fetch medicine while the nurse is briefly in the adjoining office.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Please ask the nurse when she comes back. I can't give you that.

setup.speaker: Classmate
setup.text: But you know where everything is.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: That doesn't make me qualified to use it.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The classmate waits outside the office. Mari checks that the noticeboard is straight, then checks it again.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Does that happen often?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: People see me here and assume I'm useful in every possible way.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She gives a small smile, but there is very little amusement in it.

choices.text: We can put a staff-only label on that cupboard.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: The nurse has one. It might need to be more visible.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Public information project finally finds its subject.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: A useful discovery.

choices.text: You answered clearly. I'll back you up if they ask me.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Thank you. I don't need you to argue with them.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Just say the same thing.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Yes. That would be enough.

choices.text: It would've been quicker to fetch it and let the nurse check later.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: No. The nurse needs to decide what is appropriate.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought it was a small thing.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then waiting for the right person is a small thing too.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The nurse handles the request. We finish the public noticeboard and leave the medical cupboards alone.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: I like helping here. I still want to be allowed to sit in the quiet chair sometimes.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: We should put that in the leaflet.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: Perhaps not in quite those words.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The canteen offers two desserts. Mari studies them long enough for the MC to notice.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Custard or red bean?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Which would you prefer?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I was asking you.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Ah. Of course.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She looks at the display again. The queue moves behind us.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: You choose. I don't mind either.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: It sounds easy until I notice her eyes return to the custard.

choices.text: I'm getting red bean. You can choose separately.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then... custard, please.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: There we are. Two desserts, no difficult negotiations.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I may have made that more complicated than necessary.

choices.text: Just pick one. I can't decide everything for you.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I wasn't asking you to decide everything.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It feels like you never say what you want.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I was trying not to make a small thing difficult. I see that didn't work.

choices.text: We can skip dessert if you're not in the mood.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: No, I'd like one. The custard, I think.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Custard it is.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Yes. Thank you for waiting.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We use the remaining block to review which public leaflets need replacing. Mari keeps the dessert wrapper out of the paperwork.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Worth the decision?

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: Very. I may recklessly choose the same one next time.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Her smile reaches her eyes before she lowers them to the list.

warm.speaker: Mari
warm.text: You remembered I liked the roasted tea too. I wasn't expecting you to remember.

mixed.speaker: Mari
mixed.text: I know you mean well when you ask. Sometimes I need a little time to answer.

cool.speaker: Mari
cool.text: Let's keep today simple. We can each choose for ourselves.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A class craft block becomes an opportunity to repair loose buttons on the fabric display backing. Mari has brought a small sewing kit.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You look prepared for every possible fabric emergency.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Only ordinary ones. Please don't invent a difficult one.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The MC's own blazer button comes loose while he reaches for the thread. Mari immediately sets down her work.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I can do that before it falls off.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: What about your part of the backing?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I'll finish it afterwards.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: There is already a small queue of repairs beside her.

choices.text: Thanks. You really are everyone's mum here.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Your classmate, Takahashi-kun. I'd like to stay your classmate.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant you're reliable.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: You can call me reliable. I would prefer that.

choices.text: It can wait until the backing's finished.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Put the button somewhere safe if it comes off.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Front pocket. I have a system.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then I won't interrupt your system.

choices.text: Could you show me instead? I'd like to manage the next one myself.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Slowly. The stitches don't need to be perfect; they need to hold. And please don't look at me while you're holding the needle.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: A refreshing school assessment.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Give it here. I'll show you the first stitch; you can do the rest.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: With Mari's demonstration if he requested it, or the class sewing guide if he did not, the MC secures his own button. Mari returns to her own work. His stitches are noticeably less neat than the display backing.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I think the button has character now.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: It has a great deal of thread. We can call that character.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: While we carry spare materials to the lobby, Mari receives a message asking her to collect groceries and help a sibling with homework that evening.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I should have expected that. It is their difficult subject this term.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: And you have your own assignment due.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I can do it later.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She shifts the box, trying to type an answer with her free thumb. The lid slides.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Let me set this down first.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Sorry. Yes. Thank you.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She apologizes again when a folded cloth falls out, although nobody was hurt and nothing was damaged.

choices.text: What can you realistically do tonight? You can answer with that, not the best possible version of you.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I can collect the groceries. The homework will need to be tomorrow, or someone else can help.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That sounds clear.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: It sounds strange. I'll try writing it before I change my mind.

choices.text: Can we finish the school task another day?

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: We can ask the teacher. I'd rather not quietly leave it for you.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Then we ask.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: All right.

choices.text: They need you. Your assignment can wait one night.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: It already waited last night.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't know.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: No. I haven't been saying so. That doesn't make the time appear.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We finish the carry together. Mari sends a specific reply and receives a short acknowledgment. It doesn't solve every expectation at home, but tonight now has a limit.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: I keep expecting a clear answer to sound unkind.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She reads her own message once more, then puts the phone away.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The nurse tells the student volunteers to take a break before doing anything else. Mari reaches for an untidy stack of clean blankets anyway.

setup.speaker: Nurse
setup.text: Mari. Chair first. Those can wait.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I was only going to fold the top two.

setup.speaker: Nurse
setup.text: They will survive their current condition.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Mari sits. The MC takes the other visitor chair, the one that squeaks.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I think the chair is pleased to be useful.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: You don't have to keep me company if you have something to do.

choices.text: I'll read quietly here until the break's over.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: All right. I won't ask what you're reading every thirty seconds.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'd appreciate that. I might not know yet.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: A difficult book, then.

choices.text: You worry too much. I'll make sure you rest from now on.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I don't need someone else deciding my whole day.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You weren't going to stop by yourself.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I can accept a reminder without giving up every decision.

choices.text: Would you prefer company or a little quiet on your own?

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Company. Quiet company, if that's... if that's all right. Stay where I can see you, but you don't have to keep talking.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I can attempt that.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: A brave promise, in that chair.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The break ends when the nurse checks in. Mari is tired but well; there is no collapse or romanticized illness. They finish only the assigned public materials, not extra work.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: I didn't fold a single blanket.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: A terrible afternoon for blankets.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: They seem to have managed.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A supervised open-campus activity block starts early. The MC finds Mari finishing slow aikido practice on the quiet field edge before a general exercise workshop.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I didn't know you did martial arts.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I usually practice before the house gets busy. It helps me begin the day with one thing at a time.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You're good at making it look calm.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: You didn't see the mornings when I forget which foot I'm using.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The instructor calls for everyone to put away the mats. Mari carries one, leaving the others for the group.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She catches me noticing and almost smiles.

choices.text: What do you enjoy about it when nobody needs you to be good at it?

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: The moment when the movement starts to feel continuous. I stop counting things I haven't done yet.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'd like to find something that does that for me.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: You could try the beginner session. Nobody starts graceful.

choices.text: Remind me never to annoy you. You look harmless until you do that.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I would rather you listened because I asked, not because you imagined I might hurt you.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It was supposed to be a compliment.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then tell me what you actually liked.

choices.text: Can I help carry that mat?

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: There's another one by the fence. This one's light enough.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Right. Separate jobs.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: We appear to be learning.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The workshop fills the block with ordinary beginner exercises. Mari makes a mistake in front of the group, laughs at herself and tries again.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: For once, nobody seems to need anything from her except that she enjoy being here.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We check the public reading corner after classes. Mari listens while the MC admits he has been nervous about making friends at the new school.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I keep thinking everyone else received instructions I missed.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I don't think they did. Some people are very confident while being just as confused.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Are you?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Oh, I could find you the information sheet about new-school anxiety. The nurse has—

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She stops when she sees the MC's expression.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: You were asking about me.

choices.text: Only if you feel like answering.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I am still learning what that feels like.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: We can leave the question open.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Thank you. I might come back to it.

choices.text: Yes. I don't need another leaflet. I'm interested in how you're doing.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Tired, sometimes. And relieved to be somewhere that doesn't already know who I am supposed to be.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You don't have to have a finished version ready for me.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I would like to believe that.

choices.text: You don't need to hide behind helping people. Tell me what's really wrong.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Please don't decide what my answer should be before I give it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought you needed a push.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I needed enough room to speak.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She returns the leaflet to its rack. They finish checking the reading-corner list without turning the conversation into a diagnosis or a confession.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: I was worried that if I had nothing useful to offer, I'd have nothing to say.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She has already said more than she seemed to expect. I don't ask her to prove the point again.

warm.speaker: Mari
warm.text: When I see you coming, I feel glad before I start wondering what you might need. That is new.

mixed.speaker: Mari
mixed.text: I know we keep trying to understand each other. Some days it comes more easily than others.

cool.speaker: Mari
cool.text: I can listen for a little while. I would like you to listen when I answer too.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A cooking assignment uses the canteen tables after service, under staff supervision. Everyone must plan a simple lunch for themselves.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: My little brother dislikes these mushrooms. My sister won't eat—

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She looks down at the worksheet heading.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: For myself. It says it quite clearly.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: What did you want before the household meeting began?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Mushrooms. Apparently I have been arguing against my own lunch.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She crosses out one substitution, then two.

choices.text: You could make what your siblings like and take it home. That would be more useful.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: The assignment is one meal for me.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought you'd be happier helping them.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I know. I am trying to find out what I like before somebody needs me to like something else. Just this once. Let me keep the mushrooms.

choices.text: Keep the mushrooms. You don't have to justify liking your own lunch.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then I'm keeping the ginger too.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: A dangerous wave of personal opinions.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Someone should alert the kitchen.

choices.text: Let's follow the worksheet first. We can change things after the taste test.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: A practical defense against my own habits.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Schoolwork occasionally helps.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Please don't sound too surprised. The teacher might hear.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Staff supervise the food preparation. Mari eats her own finished portion and writes a note about what she would change next time.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: More ginger.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: That seems settled.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: It is. I like knowing that.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: During independent study, Mari tells the MC she asked her family to share two evening tasks. The first conversation was awkward.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: My father said I had always managed before. I didn't know how to explain that managing and managing well weren't always the same.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Did he listen afterwards?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: A little. My mother suggested a weekly plan. My siblings were mostly concerned about who would cook.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She opens a notebook with both her homework and the household plan on separate pages.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I still feel guilty about leaving a blank space after my name.

choices.text: What would make the plan workable for you? You don't have to fill the blank just because it bothers you.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Two evenings for my own work. And one morning when I don't make everyone's lunch.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Those are things you can put on the page.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Yes. Specific things. I can ask for specific things.

choices.text: Try the plan for a week before deciding whether it works.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I can keep track of what actually happens, instead of only what I hoped would happen.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That sounds fair.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I think so too.

choices.text: Your family sounds awful. You should stop helping them completely.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I love them. I am trying to change something, not erase them.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I don't like how much they ask of you.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Neither do I, sometimes. Please let the conversation be more complicated than that.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: They use the rest of the block for their own assignments. Mari writes her available evenings on the household page before closing the notebook.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Nothing is solved by a single conversation. At least the next one will begin with something she actually wants.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The public-information project is finished for the day. Mari takes a short break by the gate before going home. A familiar neighborhood cat sleeps under a hedge.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It seems to have beaten everyone to the good seat.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: It has a strict schedule. Sleep here, sleep somewhere else, inspect people carrying food.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Did you bring anything for it?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Not today. The groundskeeper said its owner would prefer us not to feed it.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She sits on the nearby bench with empty hands. For a moment, she seems unsure what to do with them.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I can still stay a little while, can't I?

choices.text: I'll stay until the activity block ends too.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: All right. We can be available if the teacher needs the display moved.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: And otherwise do absolutely nothing useful.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: A demanding assignment.

choices.text: You look happier when you're taking care of something.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Do I need to be doing that to be good company?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant it suits you.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: It is part of me. I don't want it to be the only part you want here.

choices.text: Yes. You don't need a job to have a place on the bench.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I was hoping you would say something like that.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Should I have made it sound more impressive?

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: No. This was exactly enough.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The cat wakes, decides neither person has anything worth investigating and goes home.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: Well. We have been thoroughly assessed.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Low scores for catering.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: She laughs without hiding it this time. We remain on the bench after the cat has gone.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The nurse checks the completed reading corner and thanks both students. Mari has no extra duty assigned today.

setup.speaker: Nurse
setup.text: You can use the visitor table during the break, but go home when the block ends. Both of you.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: Understood.

setup.text: What's the plan?

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I want to make myself a cup. You may have one if you like, but I'm not going to spend the break checking whether everyone in the corridor wants tea.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: A clear plan.

response.text: I have received the necessary training.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Then I shall stop supervising. Probably.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: Thank you. I will.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: No looking guilty about it.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I'll try. You're allowed to enjoy the water without supervising me too.

choices.text: But helping everyone is what makes you special.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I don't want to earn a place with you by being endlessly available.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't say endlessly.

response.speaker: Mari
response.text: I need you to hear the difference, even when you don't mean harm.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: They drink at the visitor table and leave on time. Mari puts her own cup away last, after she has finished it.

closing.speaker: Mari
closing.text: Next time, could we talk about us? I want to answer as myself, before I worry about making the answer comfortable for you.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: I agree. She doesn't apologize for asking.

warm.speaker: Mari
warm.text: I've been choosing to spend these afternoons with you. I wanted you to know I notice that choice.

cool.speaker: Mari
cool.text: I need to say a few things plainly. I don't want to hide them inside another offer to help.

setup.text: I nearly brought a spare lunch. Ano... don't laugh. I thought you might assume I'd called you here because you looked hungry.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I might still look hungry. It isn't why I came.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She tucks a loose strand of salmon hair behind her ear. Her cup is still full.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I like you, Mari. I want to ask you out.

setup.speaker: Mari
setup.text: I know. I wanted to be able to answer without offering you something else instead.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She starts to straighten the cup, catches her hand and leaves it crooked. This time she keeps looking at him.

endings.title: Stay a Little
endings.cgBrief: Mari with a salmon feathered low ponytail and cyan eyes rests beside the infirmary visitor window with her own tea; a charcoal MC silhouette sits quietly at an equal distance beside her. Warm natural light, relaxed posture, ordinary modest uniform; she is well and awake.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: I would like that. Yes, Ren. A date. Oh... saying your name without the rest of it feels surprisingly bold.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Ren is fine. And you don't have to worry about getting every word right.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Good. You'll still have to tell me when I offer you lunch instead of answering a question. Gently, please. I'm likely to be embarrassed already.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Can we have the conversation and the food?

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She laughs, then reaches for his hand. He waits until she has offered it.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Yes. Though some days I may ask you to bring lunch.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I'll learn something that survives the trip to school.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: The nurse passes the open doorway and reminds us when the block ends. Mari answers without letting go of my hand.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Yes. Otsukaresama deshita—thank you for today. We're leaving on time. I promise.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: For the remaining few minutes, she leans back in the visitor chair and drinks her tea while it is still warm.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Stay a little. Not because I need help with anything.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I'd like that.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: She closes her eyes for one peaceful breath. I don't have to turn the moment into a promise about fixing her life. Today she has chosen something for herself, and I'm glad it includes me.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Mari / Good. Credits, then title.

endings.title: Tea for Two
endings.cgBrief: Mari and the MC silhouette share a calm tea break across two visitor chairs, balanced composition and independent cups, gentle cordial expression, open infirmary doorway in the background.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: I care about you, Takahashi-kun. But I don't want to date you. I kept trying to find a kinder sentence. I think... I think this is the kindest one I can actually mean.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I'm glad you did.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Are you all right?

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She catches the question before turning it into three more.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Disappointed. I'll be all right. You don't have to pour tea over the whole problem.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: That would be a terrible use of tea.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: We both smile, a little awkwardly. Her answer remains what it is.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: On a later school day, they meet at the visitor table after returning some public leaflets. Mari asks whether the MC wants company. He says yes.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: I brought one tea bag. The spare tin is there if you want some.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I remember where it is.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: We make our own cups. The conversation is ordinary and occasionally uneven. I don't pretend that being her friend was my plan all along, and she doesn't try to repay my disappointment by doing more for me.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: It's nice to see you.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: It's nice to see you too.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Mari / Neutral. Credits, then title.

endings.title: A Cup Left Full
endings.cgBrief: Mari calmly gathers her school bag to leave the infirmary visitor table; her full tea cup remains in the foreground, cool late light, her expression tired but resolved. No collapse, injury or helpless framing.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: I don't want to date you. I need some distance from the way things have been between us.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I thought you liked looking after me.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Sometimes I did. I wanted you to be interested in the rest of me too. When I tried to say what I needed, I often felt I was making our time together less convenient for you.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: The cup in front of her is still full. I almost tell her to drink it, then stop. She has already told me what matters.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I'm sorry. I won't try to talk you out of it.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She collects her bag. The nurse takes care of the visitor table after they leave; Mari does not stay to tidy away the conversation.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I go home without an extra lunch or an offer to check my homework. Those things were never proof that she owed me more.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Take care, Mari.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: You too.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She leaves by her own route. The MC does not follow.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Mari / Bad. Credits, then title.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: That sounded as if I was looking for someone to take care of me. I'm sorry. I want to know you, including what you need.

lines.speaker: Mari
lines.text: Then listen to this answer as mine. I don't want to earn it by being endlessly useful.
